clue.text: A lot of eggs in such a bag?

blocks.note: first meaning: a set of eggs laid at one time
second meaning: a small handbag with no handle, held in the hand

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what sort of bag would hold a big batch of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures carrying eggs in a bag; really the same word names both the batch of eggs and the kind of bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen's batch of eggs is called by this name, and so is a slim handheld evening purse.

clue.text: Vehicle, battered Polo, that is eco-friendly for commuting

definitions.text: Vehicle, battered Polo, that is eco-friendly for commuting

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the model name are rearranged

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
the Volkswagen model, taken as written

explanation.surface: A dented old VW Polo is held up as the green way to get to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a shared car, perhaps a battered Polo, is the eco-friendly way to commute.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing one vehicle among several commuters cuts emissions, which is the whole point of the arrangement.

clue.text: Mineral found in quantity, but unnamed

indicators.note: unnamed means losing the abbreviation for name, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a number is a quantity
N is the abbreviation for name, the letter to remove

explanation.surface: A mineral discovered in some quantity but not yet given a name.
explanation.walkthrough: Take NUMBER and remove N for name to leave UMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural brown earth pigment, a mineral clay containing iron and manganese oxides.

clue.text: Cabin colleague has care of chart I submitted

indicators.note: something submitted is put in, so the single letter goes inside the map word

blocks.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
to plot is to chart, and a plot is a chart or plan
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flight-deck colleague looks after the navigation chart that has been handed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabin' suggests the passenger area, but the cockpit is a cabin too; c/o on an envelope is the convention behind the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The second pilot shares the cockpit, the cabin at the front of a plane, with the captain.

clue.text: Is rude about area transport

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
buses are a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Someone is grumbling about the local bus service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sits inside the definition rather than signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse someone is to insult them or speak rudely of them.

clue.text: Filled with air, became very angry

blocks.note: first meaning: inflated, as a balloon
second meaning: lost one's temper explosively

explanation.surface: Someone puffed up and then flew into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to inflate something and to lose one's temper, both past tense here.

clue.text: Bank account details the police may take

blocks.note: first meaning: the periodic summary sent by a bank
second meaning: a witness's formal account recorded by officers

explanation.surface: Officers investigating a crime may seize someone's bank records.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank sends a printed record of transactions, and police record a witness's formal written account; both share the name.

clue.text: Attendant chucked waste on road

indicators.note: chucked suggests thrown about, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: An attendant dumps rubbish onto the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an attendant, for example one who looks after passengers on a ship or plane.

clue.text: Need to go to ground in England, for CID are circling

indicators.note: circling means moving round and round, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Detectives circle round in England, looking for someone who has gone to ground.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detective branch; here its letters join the others for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft makes an emergency touchdown when it is compelled by trouble to come down.

clue.text: Grumble – this apple is sour

blocks.note: first meaning: to complain or find fault
second meaning: a small sour wild apple

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the apple they bit is sour.
explanation.definitionFit: To crab is to carp or complain, and the crab apple is a small, very tart wild fruit.

clue.text: One doesn't want to sit through a whole concert?

definitions.text: One doesn't want to sit through a whole concert?

blocks.clueFragment: One doesn't want to sit through a whole concert?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone impatient who leaves a concert early
setter's reading: a person who chooses to stand for the whole performance

explanation.walkthrough: At the BBC Proms in London's Royal Albert Hall, cheap tickets are for standing in the arena; those who stand are named after the old promenade concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular at the Proms stands rather than sits, by choice, throughout each concert.

clue.text: As one of three subjects, writing in pink pen

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other, so the subject's letter sits within the colour

blocks.note: coral is a pinkish colour

blocks.clueFragment: As one of three subjects, writing
blocks.note: the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so writing is one R

explanation.surface: A schoolchild practises one of the basic subjects, writing, using a pink pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like the writing tool but is the enclosure for animals; R goes inside CORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is a fenced enclosure for livestock, just as a pen is.

clue.text: Car's first off, about to take advantage of high road

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is kept
about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the opening letter of car
off as in gone, departed
to use someone is to take advantage of them

explanation.surface: A driver sets off first and makes the most of a raised road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'first off', but it stands alone as the outer piece, meaning gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a road raised above wet ground or water, literally a high road.

clue.text: Pressure on freedom of action is commonplace

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
latitude is scope or freedom to act

explanation.surface: Putting pressure on people's freedom to act has become routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A commonplace, used as a noun, is a trite remark, the same thing as a banal saying.

clue.text: The pothole not hard to snap with this lens?

definitions.note: the answer is the type of lens, used here as a noun for one

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the following letter from the phrase
to snap is to break, and the broken letters are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A photographer wants to take a picture of a pothole and wonders which lens to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' looks like taking a photo but signals the rearrangement; remove one H from THE POTHOLE before shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto is a long-focus camera lens that magnifies distant subjects.

clue.text: Make one's way with purpose

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Someone sets off with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with purpose' reads as one phrase describing the travel, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To wend is to go or travel, as in wending one's way home.

clue.text: Move about in confusion in factory

blocks.note: first meaning: to wander aimlessly in a crowd
second meaning: a manufacturing works

explanation.surface: Workers wander aimlessly around a muddled factory floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowds mill around when shuffling about aimlessly, and a cotton or paper works is also called by this name.

clue.text: Children's game lost by the witless

blocks.note: first meaning: the game played with small glass balls
second meaning: one's wits, in the idiom of losing them

explanation.surface: A child's game that only fools lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Children flick small glass balls in this game, and someone gone mad is said to have lost them, an idiom for sanity.

clue.text: A refund from the government, after you submit this?

definitions.text: A refund from the government, after you submit this?

blocks.note: surface reading: money handed back by the state
setter's reading: the annual form sent in declaring income

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a refund is the thing itself; really the answer is the form whose submission might bring money back.
explanation.definitionFit: The yearly declaration of income to the revenue authorities, which may lead to a rebate.

clue.text: See further military action, but not the front line

blocks.note: first meaning: to serve again
second meaning: troops held back from the front

explanation.surface: A soldier goes back into combat, though away from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-serve it means serve again, and the reserve is the body of troops kept back from battle.

clue.text: Overcharging done in the daylight?

blocks.note: surface reading: setting prices too high
setter's reading: the idiom for a blatant rip-off, a theft in broad daylight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Daylight' points to the idiom 'daylight' plus the answer, used of shamelessly excessive prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A grossly inflated price is called a daylight theft, an idiom for blatant overcharging.

clue.text: Stick nose in, announcing award

indicators.note: announcing is saying something out loud, so we want the word's sound, not spelling

blocks.note: a medal is an award

explanation.surface: A nosy person barges in to announce who has won a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere in other people's business is to poke one's nose in where it is not wanted.

clue.text: Stunning, rude dismissal

blocks.note: first meaning: as in ... gorgeous
second meaning: an insolent way to tell someone to go away

explanation.surface: A shocking, impolite sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means strikingly attractive, and as an exclamation it is an offensive brush-off.

clue.text: Regularly sick, chafes in prison

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first and third letters of sick
to chafe is to rub

explanation.surface: An inmate is constantly ill and irritated in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a well-known prison in west London, often just called Scrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the short name of a London jail, so it stands for a prison.

clue.text: Goes round in luxury car

blocks.note: first meaning: turns over and over
second meaning

explanation.surface: Someone tours about in a posh motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball turns over as it travels, and the British luxury marque Rolls-Royce is commonly shortened to this.

clue.text: One's voluntary contribution to the NHS may be of various types

definitions.text: One's voluntary contribution to the NHS may be of various types

blocks.clueFragment: One's voluntary contribution to the NHS
blocks.note: surface reading: a charitable gift of money to the health service
setter's reading: groups A, B, AB and O

explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service. 'Types' points to blood groups rather than kinds of donation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who freely gives their blood to the health service, which may be any of several groups.

clue.text: Returning ship, poetically, is a national symbol

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: in poetry a keel can stand for a whole ship

explanation.surface: A homecoming ship is held up as an emblem of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The leek is the national emblem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable is the traditional emblem of Wales, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: Tool in small shed

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a hovel is a shed or wretched hut

explanation.surface: A gardening implement kept in a little shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a digging implement with a broad blade.

clue.text: Top cow?

blocks.note: first meaning: a knitted pullover
second meaning: a dairy breed from the Channel Islands

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top cow' suggests a champion animal; split it into two meanings. A jersey is the British word for a pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover worn on the upper body, and also a breed of cattle from the Channel Island of the same name.
